info.name: Coach HQ API
info.description:
Coach HQ endpoints, generated from ui/api/ on 2026-09-04.

AUTH: every request except Waitlist needs the `coach_session` cookie. It is HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax, so you cannot read it from JS and you cannot use plain http.

To get one:
1. Sign in to the deployment in a browser (Preview or Production).
2. DevTools -> Application -> Cookies -> pick `coach_session`.
3. Copy its value into this collection's `sessionCookie` variable.
4. Run `Auth / me` to confirm it works before anything else.

The cookie rotates (ADR 0009). If requests start 401ing, re-copy it.

WARNING - three requests here commit to GitHub, and `baseUrl` defaults to production.
- coach-message and coach-chat WRITE to the athlete's repo, on branch `process.env.COACH_CHAT_BRANCH ?? "main"`. Unless COACH_CHAT_BRANCH is set on the deployment you are hitting, a test call commits to the athlete's real `main` and overwrites user_data/coach/latest_message.json.
- Waitlist WRITES to this HQ repo (platform/waitlist.json) and needs no cookie, so it is the one you can fire without meaning to.

Everything else is read-only. Auth / logout writes nothing but ends the session, so run it last.

variable.description: Production, or paste a Vercel Preview URL. Must be https - the session cookie is Secure.
Value of the coach_session cookie, copied from browser DevTools.
Must satisfy isStrictActivityId: strava:<digits> or healthkit:<UUID>. Must exist in the athlete repo.
Only for Auth / refresh, which is the iOS path and is NOT cookie-authed. iOS holds this in Keychain; there is no way to read one out of a browser.

request.description: Start here. If this 401s, the cookie is wrong or expired and nothing else will work.
repo-file returns 400 'No repo resolved yet' until this has run for the session.

item.name: refresh - iOS token exchange (POST, not cookie-authed)

request.description: handleRefresh (auth/[...action].ts) is POST-only and 405s on GET. The session cookie is not its auth - possession of a valid refresh_token is, which is why no Cookie header is sent. This exists for iOS, which keeps its refresh_token in Keychain; a browser session cannot produce one, so leave this request alone unless you have a token to test with.
Redirects to GitHub. Open in a browser; Postman will not complete the OAuth round trip usefully.

item.name: logout - run this LAST, it kills the session

request.description:
Clears coach_session and 302s to /. Postman follows the redirect by default, so a 200 with the app's HTML is the success case here, not a failure.

Running this invalidates the value in `sessionCookie` - every other request starts 401ing until you sign in again and re-copy it.

The endpoint the OpenRouter pilot moves. No sync needed - it is a plain POST.

Body contract is strict (validateActivityIdsPayload): exactly one key, `activity_ids`, an array of 1..MAX_ACTIVITY_IDS strict ids. Any extra key is a 400.

WRITES user_data/coach/latest_message.json in the athlete repo. Set COACH_CHAT_BRANCH on the deployment first if you do not want that on main.

Expected 200: {"message": "...", "delivered": true}
502 'Gemini returned invalid JSON' was the #827 bug. 502 'Gemini truncated its response before finishing (MAX_TOKENS...)' is the post-fix, honest version.
Expect 400 'Request body must contain only activity_ids'. Cheap way to confirm you are hitting the real route and not a cached shell.
Read-only - the same route, dispatched on method (coach-chat.ts's handle()). The cheapest way to see what a POST turn actually committed, without spending a model call.
Cheapest real chat call. `onboardingHints` is optional.
`messages` is prior turns, `knownSha` guards the commit. WRITES to the athlete repo.
Reads user_data/coach/latest_message.json among other things - handy for confirming what a coach-message call actually wrote.
gen/dashboard_snapshot.json via the GitHub Contents API. Run Auth / list-my-repos first or this 400s.

The only unauthenticated route here - no cookie needed, which is exactly why it is easy to fire by accident.

WRITES: appends {email, created_at, source} to platform/waitlist.json and commits it to WAITLIST_GITHUB_REPO, which defaults to sibling-shipyard/coach-phelps-hq - this repo, not an athlete's. With baseUrl left at production, sending this puts test@example.com in the real waitlist and you clean it up by hand.

Body is {email, source?}; `website` is a honeypot field - set it and the route silently accepts and discards the signup.
